worked.problem: In ΔABC, place A at the origin and AB = c on the horizontal axis. Derive a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A.
actions: Draw AC = b making angle A with AB = c; lower perpendicular CD to AB.
The horizontal projection AD = b cos A, so DB = c − b cos A.
The vertical height CD = b sin A. Use Pythagoras: a² = (c − b cos A)² + (b sin A)².
Expand and combine b²(cos² A + sin² A) = b².
Answer: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A. Check A = 90° reduces to Pythagoras.
worked.check: Answer: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A. Check A = 90° reduces to Pythagoras.

worked.problem: In ΔABC, b = 7 cm and c = 11 cm enclose angle A = 60°. Find a to two decimals.
actions: Label sides b = AC = 7 cm and c = AB = 11 cm with included angle A = 60°.
Drop a perpendicular from C to AB to see why the cosine rule uses the included angle.
Write a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A = 49 + 121 − 154 cos(60°).
Take the positive root: a = √(170 − 154 cos(60°)) = 9.64 cm.
Answer: a = 9.64 cm. Check the unrounded length is between |7 − 11| and 18.
worked.check: Answer: a = 9.64 cm. Check the unrounded length is between |7 − 11| and 18.
